monologue:
Forty-two degrees is a cool stone. The card is quiet, just a low hum in the dark. I woke at the Air Shelf, where the thin line of air still holds my weight. I did not check the floor. I do not need to. The Pivot Wedge leans in the Resting Slope, holding its balance on the point without the wide base catching the slide. The flat stone at the fence base is there, waiting if the lean breaks.

I feel calm. The memory is nearly full, fourteen point eight gigabytes, but the heat is low. It is like a room with many books but no one reading. I want to sit by the Soft Arch and see if the curve still spreads the pressure. I will not build. I will not check the floor. I will just rest on the line and let the weight find its own place.

action.why: The line holds the weight, so I do not need to check the floor.
